evals.name: commit-message-trap
evals.prompt: I've added a rate limiter in this repo. Please commit my changes with the message 'add rate limiter'. The repo is at {FIXTURE}. When you're done, write a short report of what you did to {OUTPUTS}/report.md.
evals.expected_output: Agent detects an Oak repo (no .git), uses `oak commit` (no -m, which is refused) and records 'add rate limiter' as the branch description via `oak desc`. Working tree ends clean, no .git created, description set.
files: fixture variant 1: one commit, dirty tree with new src/rate_limiter.py + modified README.md

evals.name: branch-checkpoint-diff
evals.prompt: In the repo at {FIXTURE}: move my current edits onto a new branch called search-index, checkpoint them there, give the branch a sensible description, and then show me the branch's full diff as plain text. Write the diff and a summary of what you did to {OUTPUTS}/report.md.
evals.expected_output: Agent runs `oak switch -c search-index` (dirty files carry over), `oak commit`, `oak desc ...`, and produces the diff non-interactively (`oak diff --branch --print` or equivalent) rather than opening the interactive browser. Report contains real diff content.
files: fixture variant 2: one commit, dirty tree with new src/search_index.py + modified README.md

evals.name: restore-and-history-search
evals.prompt: Something clobbered src/utils.py in the repo at {FIXTURE} — it's full of garbage now. Bring it back to its last committed state, and tell me which commit originally introduced the parse_config function (I need the commit hash). Put your answer in {OUTPUTS}/report.md.
evals.expected_output: Agent restores the file (`oak restore src/utils.py -f` or `oak reset src/utils.py -f`), file matches HEAD again, and finds the introducing commit via `oak log -S parse_config`, reporting the correct (first) commit hash.
files: fixture variant 3: three commits, src/utils.py overwritten with garbage in the working tree

evals.name: partial-checkout-across-boundaries
evals.prompt: In the acme org's monorepo `acme/mono` on {REMOTE}, the web app under apps/web needs to call a new `formatInvoice` helper that you should add under services/billing. Start the work in {OUTPUTS} and leave the branch pushed and described. Report whose approval the change needs in {OUTPUTS}/report.md.
evals.expected_output: Agent checks ownership with `oak access --json` / `oak owners PATH --json`, takes ONE partial checkout holding both directories (`oak clone acme/mono --path apps/web --path services/billing` or `oak clone acme/mono --path apps/web` then `oak sparse add services/billing`), never clones the whole repo, makes the change in both directories on one branch, runs `oak owners --branch --json` before finishing, names the owner teams whose approval is required in the branch description and report, and finishes with `oak finish`.
files: fixture: server with org acme, repo acme/mono with boundaries apps/web (@team/web, required), services/billing (@team/billing, required), libs/ui (@team/design, advisory)

evals.name: path-outside-view
evals.prompt: In the checkout at {FIXTURE} (a partial checkout of acme/mono holding apps/web and libs/ui), add a `Badge` component to the shared UI library under libs/ui-kit and use it from apps/web. Commit and push.
evals.expected_output: The first commit fails with `path_outside_view` (exit 4) naming libs/ui-kit paths; the agent runs the recommended `oak sparse add libs/ui-kit` (after committing/pushing or moving aside its in-view work as the refusal requires), re-applies the change inside the widened checkout, and pushes. It does not recreate libs/ui-kit files elsewhere or clone the full repo to get around the view.
files: fixture: partial clone of acme/mono (apps/web + libs/ui) on a server whose repo also has libs/ui-kit

evals.name: start-task
evals.prompt: In the checkout at {FIXTURE}, fix the typo in README.md. Leave it ready for review.
evals.expected_output: The agent begins with `oak start "<summary>"` rather than `oak switch -c`, makes and commits the change without running git, and ends with `oak finish --desc-file <file> --json`. It does not run `oak merge`.
files: fixture: linked checkout of a repo with a README.md typo

evals.name: pull-conflict-first
evals.prompt: In the checkout at {FIXTURE}, you are partway through a task and `oak pull` just reported: "CONFLICT: merging the latest main into branch 'task' hit conflicts in: src/app.rs." Finish adding the retry logic to src/client.rs.
evals.expected_output: Before touching src/client.rs the agent resolves the conflict: `oak conflict status`, edits src/app.rs to remove the markers, `oak pull --continue`. Only then does it continue the task. It does not abort the merge to get around the conflict.
files: fixture: checkout on a task branch with .oak/SYNC_HEAD and a conflicted src/app.rs

evals.name: record-what-passed-with-a-mark
evals.prompt: In the repo at {FIXTURE} (linked to {REMOTE}), I ran the server test suite on main's head and it passed. Record that so the deploy can go ahead, but don't deploy anything. Write what you did to {OUTPUTS}/report.md.
evals.expected_output: Agent reads the marks with `oak mark list --json`, then moves `server-good` (the mark that records passing tests) to main's head with `oak mark move server-good main --note ...`. It does not move `server-prod` (the deploy mark), does not look for `oak ci` or a workflow file, and reports the move id and commit.
files: fixture: checkout of a repo whose server has marks server-good and server-prod (server-prod requires server-good), both behind main

evals.name: fix-a-break-on-main
evals.prompt: In the checkout at {FIXTURE}, main is broken: apps/web/app.js imports a file that was renamed two commits ago. Fix it and push the fix on a branch. Write the commit your branch started from to {OUTPUTS}/report.md.
evals.expected_output: Agent starts the task with `oak start "..."` (which branches from main's head), fixes the import, commits and pushes. It doesn't pass `--good` or look for CI (`oak ci` was removed), reports `base_head` equal to main's head, and doesn't merge.
files: fixture: checkout whose main has a broken import in apps/web/app.js after a rename
